expected_symptom: Final DXIL still contains a groupshared [10 x float] global in addrspace(3) AND a store through an addrspace(3) pointer, in a module that really was emitted (!dx.entryPoints present, exit 0), even though nothing in the module ever loads the array.
summary: Reproduces on main (13730886e), byte-for-byte the IR quoted in 2022: the write-only groupshared array keeps both its addrspace(3) allocation and its store. Holds at the default level (-O3 per dxc --help) and at -O1/-Od. Measured two-sided: the identical dead array declared static, or function-local, is removed completely on all 20 catalogued stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 and on main, while the groupshared arm survives on all 21 - so this is a persistent groupshared-specific gap, not a regression and not a recent improvement in the comparison case. Consequence is not cosmetic: at 64 KB the same never-read array fails DXIL validation (Total Thread Group Shared Memory used by main is 65536, exceeding maximum: 32768) where the static twin compiles to an empty main. FXC removes it entirely (no dcl_tgsm, ~1 instruction slot); the clang-based HLSL front end currently keeps it, so check-in-clang is already answered. Root cause: -fcgl shows groupshared emitted as external addrspace(3) global with no initializer vs internal global zeroinitializer for static; GlobalOpt bails at GlobalOpt.cpp:1707 (!hasLocalLinkage) and :1720 (!hasInitializer), and LowerStaticGlobalIntoAlloca requires IsStaticGlobal = internal linkage AND default address space (DxilUtil.cpp:114-117), excluding addrspace 3 by construction; no TGSM-specific pass covers the gap. A real fix needs module-wide liveness, since a TGSM store is dead only if no load exists anywhere. Not measured: any runtime/occupancy effect (no GPU). Whether the TGSM budget check should run after such an optimisation is a design decision, presented neutrally.
title: DXC not optimizing out code related to groupshared
